title: The Roman Custom of Charity
english: For it is your custom from the beginning to do good to all brothers in various ways, and to send supplies to many churches throughout the whole city; in this way you refresh the poor who are in need, and in this way you provide for brothers who are in metal [wealth].

Through these you send the first supplies, a custom handed down from fathers which Romans preserve among Romans; which not only your blessed bishop Soter maintained, but also increased, providing the abundance sent out to the saints, and with blessed words encouraging the suffering brothers as a fatherly, loving parent does.

In this letter also he mentions the letter of Clement to the Corinthians, declaring from of old that it is the custom to perform the reading of it for the church. He says, therefore: We lead the present Lord's Day, the holy day, in which we read your letter; which we shall always have reading to be admonished, just as we had the former written to us through Clement.
